title: Traffic Shock Waveproof Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working-playbook is focused on planning and executing a 'waveproof' rollout strategy to survive sudden traffic shocks (10x spikes, traffic pattern anomalies, and bursty traffic from integrations). Rather than a generic launch checklist, this centers on telemetry-driven hold points, automated throttle + fallback policies, and on-call choreography to preserve SLOs while we gather telemetry and scale safely.

Summary & Goals:
- Primary goal: Keep 95th percentile latency under 600ms and error rate under 0.5% during a 10x traffic spike for page-load style inference routes.
- Secondary goals: Maintain cost delta within +35% of baseline for first 24h, ensure no PII exfiltration during degraded modes, and validate fallback quality is acceptable to product owners.

Key KPI definitions (observable + formula):
- Request TPS (observed): sum(requests)/60s
- 95p latency (ms): latency distribution -> value at 95th percentile
- Error rate (%): failed_requests / total_requests * 100
- Backend saturated GPUs: count(gpu_utilization>95%) over 1m windows
- Cost per 1k tokens: billing.tokens / (requests*avg_tokens) * 1000

Thresholds and guardrails (hold criteria):
- Green -> 95p latency < 350ms, error rate < 0.2%, GPU saturation < 70%
- Yellow -> 350ms <= 95p latency < 600ms OR error rate between 0.2%-0.5% OR GPU saturation 70-90% => slow ramp + enable KV cache warmup
- Red -> 95p latency >= 600ms OR error rate >= 0.5% OR GPU saturation > 90% => enter containment (step down traffic + fallback)

Traffic ramp plan (percentage/time):
- Step 0 (smoke): 0.1% traffic, 15m observation, must be green
- Step 1 (probe): 1% traffic, 30m observation, check artifacts
- Step 2 (ramp): 10% traffic, 60m observation, autoscale policy engaged
- Step 3 (burst test): 25% traffic, 2h observation, validate fallbacks
- Step 4 (open): remove throttle only after 24h stable telemetry

Automated controls & rules (runtime hooks):
- Circuit policy: detect P99 latency increase >2x over baseline within 5m -> route 30% of new requests to model-compact variant and enable streaming partial responses
- Throttle policy: if TPS increase >300% in 1m, throttle new sessions by token-bucket algorithm to target a 40% acceptance rate until metrics return green
- Cache warming: on canary completion trigger prefix cache fill for top-1000 prompts

Fallback variants and quality tradeoffs (owner: Product ML):
- Primary: model-v1 (full context, highest quality)
- Fallback A: model-v1-quant8 (cheaper, minor quality diffs)
- Fallback B: model-v0.9-small (fast, lower quality) -> used only after autoscale exhaustion
- Fallback C: canned responses for edge routes (last-resort, must be audited)

Runbook (immediate steps when Yellow/Red):
- Yellow: notify oncall (pager), open 'traffic-shock' triage doc, increment max replicas by 20% if GPUs available, enable extra logging for top 10 slow endpoints (owner: infra)
- Red: engage incident lead, initiate traffic rollback to previous safe percentage, switch 30% traffic to fallback variant, schedule immediate capacity:manual allocation with infra (owner: SRE + infra lead)
- Post-incident: create postmortem with signal timeline, annotate runbook gaps, and schedule a retro with product and ML authors

Monitoring / Dashboards to watch (links in linked_artifacts page):
- Live dashboard: prodops/traffic-waveproof: TPS, 95/99 latencies, error rates, GPU saturation by pool, model fallback ratio, KV-cache hit rate
- Alert rules: Error rate > 0.5% for 3m; 95p latency > 600ms for 5m; GPU saturation > 95% for 2m

Staffing & roles during rollout:
- Incident lead (IL): Emily Park - coordinates comms and decisions
- Oncall SRE: rotation -> primary + secondary mailbox
- Product owner: Priya Nair - decision authority for quality vs availability tradeoffs
- ML lead: Luca Romero - approves fallback variants and quality thresholds
- Engineering support: Jonas Müller - capacity ops + infra run commands

Pre-launch checklist (must be completed before Step 1):
- Autoscaling policies validated in staging and test harness (ticket: ENG-4321)
- Canary route + synthetic load test script committed and smoke green locally
- Fallback variants uploaded and verified for contract compatibility
- Dashboards created and shared with stakeholders, alerts mapped to oncall
- Security review: verify KMS keys for private deployments and confirm logging PII filters

Open questions / known risks:
- Unknown integration patterns from partner X could generate many tiny sessions (session explosion). Need to run partner-specific load test.
- Cost model under fallback (quant8) still approximate — finance to provide 48h estimate for committed capacity.

Post-launch telemetry audit (72h & 7-day checkpoints):
- 72h: verify SLO burn vs expected, compare actual fallback percent vs simulated
- 7d: retention analysis, cost delta vs baseline, convert any long-tail errors to bugs/tickets

Next steps (action items):
- [Priya] finalize canary script and hand to Jonas by 2025-02-18
- [Luca] run partner X session-mode test and upload results to linked_artifacts by 2025-02-20
- [Emily] add temporary alert escalation for this rollout window and confirm pager routing by 2025-02-17

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep runbook light and decisive; avoid multi-step approvals when metrics clearly show red
- Bake a simple scoring for fallback quality to help product decide when to accept degraded outputs

This doc is intentionally operational and terse — use it as the canonical plan for traffic shock scenarios in the next dedicated and hosted launches. Update linked_artifacts with the finalized dashboards and the incident runbook after the first rollout attempt.
